scope: Proposition 2.2 (Uniform bound for complete splitting) of the manuscript “Primitive roots for every admissible integer base” (preprints/Primitive-roots-for-every-admissible-integer-base-October-4-2026/primitive-roots-all-integer-bases.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 029 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 671ac4b3ece879f6), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 6. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix an integer a with |a| > 1, and put δ0 = 10−6. For all sufficiently large real x and all primes q sufficiently large in terms of a, with q ≤ exp(L0.3), one has #{p prime : x < p ≤ 2x, p splits completely in Kq} ≪a x q(q − 1)L + x1−δ0 . (2.4) The implied constant and the threshold for x are independent of q. For a = 2, every prime q ≥ 5 is allowed, with absolute constants and an absolute threshold for x.
